candidate.title: FRISCR
candidate.scope: The FRISCR row of the assigned Illumina schematic: fixed single-cell RNA recovery followed by the depicted cDNA, PCR and Nextera-style indexed fragment-library preparation. The left Fixed single cell to RNA illustration summarizes the target; it is not a transfer into the later cell suspension. The visible Smart-seq2, snRNA-seq and CEL-Seq rows and the right chemical legend are neighboring context, not alternatives of this card. SmartSeq2 is an embedded preparation component, not an additional target method. The material graph ends at the indexed cDNA library; sequencing is discussed only to interpret what that library can report. The primary implementation clarifies the bead-release and sorting interfaces, without expanding the drawn blocks into laboratory recipes.

method_scopes.rationale: All nine operations belong to the single labelled FRISCR route. The primary article describes FRISCR as RNA recovery from fixed, permeabilized, stained, sorted single cells, followed by SmartSeq2 cDNA preparation and Nextera XT library generation. The downstream named subprotocols are components of this depicted implementation. The paper’s live-cell validation and Triton-X100 controls are not drawn alternatives and do not add workflow targets. The left target vignette summarizes fixed-cell RNA recovery rather than supplying a second RNA-to-cell transfer; enzyme icons are reagents and the row has no depicted split or pooling.
